label: input h/x/e in the original phase after a preceding x/v/o/n/e/m/i/r/g
explanation: A sparse candidate-high unit (about 1% of steps). Around 70% of its activation mass falls in the original phase, where it responds mostly to the input tokens h (9x lift, 33% of mass), x and e (5x each). Activation depends on context: it is much more likely when the previous input is one of x, v, o, n, e, m, i, r, g, somewhat more likely early in the sequence (t=1-3), and less likely once digits have appeared (no-digit sequences have 1.4x lift). It never fires at t=0 and almost never on the <DEL> step. The remaining ~30% of mass is in the copy phase, concentrated at recall_idx=1, the step whose input is the echoed first original token. This includes the largest activations, e.g. when the first token is h, 2, y or x and the output is p/q/2. A bare h/x/e input test is imprecise (precision 0.13, mass recall 0.61). Adding the previous-token condition raises dev F1 to 0.41 (precision 0.37, mass recall 0.54). Adding the copy-phase recall_idx=1 clause did not improve F1. Many h/x/e inputs in the right context still do not fire, so the unit reads a distributed hidden-state code that these token conditions only partly capture.
